title: Matrix calculus for layers and losses
goal: Differentiate scalar losses with respect to vectors and matrices, keeping track of shapes with the chain rule and trace identities.
exercises: Find ∇f for f(x) = xᵀAx with A = [[1, 4], [0, 2]] at x = (1, 2). Compare it with 2Ax.
Find the gradient of ‖Ax − b‖² for A = [[1, 0], [0, 1], [1, 1]], b = (1, 2, 0) at x = (1, 1).
A linear layer Y = XW + 1bᵀ has X = [[1, 2], [3, 0], [0, 1]], W = [[2, 0], [1, 1]] and upstream gradient G = [[1, 0], [0, 1], [1, −1]]. Compute ∂L/∂W, ∂L/∂b and ∂L/∂X, and check each shape.
For f in Exercise 1, compute the central and the forward difference for ∂f/∂x₁ with h = 0.1. Why is the central difference exact here?
solutions: A + Aᵀ = [[2, 4], [4, 4]], so ∇f = (A + Aᵀ)x = (2 + 8, 4 + 8) = (10, 12). Check with f = x₁² + 4x₁x₂ + 2x₂²: ∂f/∂x₁ = 2x₁ + 4x₂ = 10 and ∂f/∂x₂ = 4x₁ + 4x₂ = 12. The shortcut 2Ax = 2(9, 4) = (18, 8) is wrong because A is not symmetric.

f(1, 2) = 1 + 8 + 8 = 17, f(1.1, 2) = 18.01 and f(0.9, 2) = 16.01. Central: (18.01 − 16.01)/0.2 = 10, exactly the true value. Forward: (18.01 − 17)/0.1 = 10.1, an error of 0.1 = h·(∂²f/∂x₁²)/2 = 0.1·2/2. The central difference is exact because f is quadratic in x₁: the even-order terms cancel in f(x + h) − f(x − h), and there is no third derivative.
checkpoint: Derive ∂L/∂W, ∂L/∂X and ∂L/∂b for a linear layer from dL = tr(Gᵀ dY), justify every transpose by its shape, and design a finite-difference check with a sensible step size.
